shoulderConstruction.verdict: MODIFIED (SEMI-) DROPPED SHOULDER — extended shoulder, scooped armhole, low flat cap with no ease
shoulderConstruction.confidence: MEDIUM — construction type from 2D geometry; the drop relative to the natural shoulder is not determinable
evidence: Shoulder point 25.3 cm from CB = level with the chest line (back half-width at the underarm 25.5 cm) and 4.3 cm outside the narrowest across-back line (42.0 cm wide, 6.0 cm above the underarm). A set-in shoulder point sits well inside the chest line.
Armhole is curved, not straight: back edge 26.9 cm on a 23.7 cm chord, bowing up to 45 mm inward (front 41 mm, 41 mm); the scoop is at the underarm — a set-in-style armhole curve.

Sleeve cap height 9.5 cm over a cap base of 47.1 cm (ratio 0.20); cap edges within 19 mm of their chords. Cap height / armhole depth = 0.31. A low, flat cap belongs to a dropped / extended shoulder; a set-in jacket sleeve needs a much higher cap.
Cap seam 51.4 cm vs armhole 51.8 cm → cap ease -0.3 cm: no set-in ease.
Shoulder seam 17.1 cm (back edge), slope 22.7° from horizontal.
shoulderConstruction.shoulderSeamPosition: HPS 9.5 cm from CB → shoulder point 25.3 cm from CB (back), 17.1 cm, 22.7° slope; the sleeve cap peak meets it there.
shoulderConstruction.armholeShape: Curved, scooped at the underarm (narrowest back 42.0 cm, front CF→armhole 21.1 cm), widening to the shoulder point; deep (30.3 cm).
shoulderConstruction.sleeveHeadShape: Low, flat cap: 9.5 cm high on a 47.1 cm base, no ease.
shoulderConstruction.dropRelativeToNaturalShoulder: NOT DETERMINABLE from the pattern (no avatar, POMList empty). The pattern shows the shoulder point extended 4.3 cm beyond the across-back line — a geometric indicator only, not SC-1.
shoulderConstruction.implication: Same family as JACKETEK K1 (dropped shoulder) but a milder drop with a curved armhole. JACKETEK B09 59.5 cm vs purchased 50.6 cm combines the size difference (B01 51.0 vs 62) and the different amount of drop — they cannot be separated without the natural-shoulder reference. SC-1 and B09 stay unchanged.

shoulderExtension.name: Dropped-shoulder extension per side
shoulderExtension.status: JACKETEK DEVELOPMENT RULE (approved for development use 2026-10-11) — validated by the pattern maker and the M sample; NOT production approved
shoulderExtension.rule: JACKETEK across shoulder (size) = Golden Bear set-in across shoulder (size) + 2 × 5.0 cm. Constant extension for every size unless a pattern constraint requires otherwise.
shoulderExtension.replaces: REJECTED / REPLACED — not an active rule: the earlier proposal of 3.0 cm per side (B09 / B01 ≈ 0.895) was rejected by JACKETEK on 2026-10-11 because it under-represents the dropped-shoulder proportion of the canonical S.i.-based JACKETEK flat.
why: Golden Bear supplies the set-in shoulder width and its grading; the dropped shoulder moves the shoulder point outwards by the extension on each side.
JACKETEK's visual reading of the canonical S.i.-based flat: shoulder-point width ≈ 0.96 × half-chest width for the M silhouette → 0.96 × 62.0 = 59.5 cm, which matches 49.53 + 2 × 5.0 = 59.53 cm.

The S.i. flat is a proportional / visual reference only: no drawing unit is converted to cm. (Recorded for transparency: a landmark measurement on the stylised drawing gives shoulder-point span ÷ chest width ≈ 1.20; the drawing is not to scale and neither ratio is a measurement.)
The pattern maker and the M sample validate the rule; a pattern constraint may require a different extension, proposed explicitly.
